title: Target Earnings Beat Estimates as Sales Rise 7.1% and Guidance Rises
excerpt: Target earned $2.65 a share on $27.07 billion in sales, beating the Zacks consensus on both lines as comparable sales rose 5.6% on 5% traffic growth — and raised its full-year sales and earnings guidance ahead of the holidays.
body:
• Target beat estimates on both lines: GAAP and adjusted earnings of $2.65 per share against the $2.05 Zacks consensus, on net sales of $27.07 billion, up 7.1 percent, against $26.36 billion expected.
  • Comparable sales rose 5.6 percent as comparable traffic grew 5.0 percent — store comparable sales up 4.6 percent and digital comparable sales up 9.8 percent.
  • Tariff refunds added $0.50 a share. Excluding them, adjusted earnings of $2.15 still beat the consensus and rose 21 percent year over year.
  • Target raised its full-year guidance — net sales growth around 6 percent and earnings of $10.65 to $11.40 a share — and heads into the holidays with more than 8,000 new gifts, over half exclusive to Target, including thousands priced at $5 and under.

Target Corporation beat Wall Street estimates on both lines Wednesday, reporting third-quarter earnings of $2.65 a share on net sales of $27.1 billion and raising its full-year guidance. The quarter ended October 31.

The company reported GAAP and adjusted earnings per share of $2.65, compared with GAAP EPS of $1.51 and adjusted EPS of $1.78 a year earlier, according to its earnings release. Net earnings rose 75.8 percent to $1.21 billion. Analysts surveyed by Zacks had expected earnings of $2.05 a share on net sales of $26.36 billion, Zacks reported.

Traffic drove the sales beat

Comparable sales grew 5.6 percent, against a decline of 2.7 percent in the year-ago quarter, as comparable traffic rose 5.0 percent while the average transaction amount rose 0.6 percent, according to Zacks. Comparable store sales increased 4.6 percent and comparable digital sales 9.8 percent, the company said.

Growth was broad. Fun 101 sales grew nearly 27 percent, Beauty sales more than 9 percent, and Food and Beverage sales nearly 7 percent. Merchandise sales rose 6.9 percent to $26.45 billion, while non-merchandise sales rose 19.3 percent on growth in Roundel advertising revenue, Target Circle Card profit-sharing revenue, Target Circle 360 membership revenue and the Target+ marketplace.

"Our third-quarter results reflect continued progress against our strategic priorities, centered on serving busy families with our signature blend of style, design and value."

— Michael Fiddelke, Chief Executive Officer, Target

Tariff refunds lifted profit — but did not create the beat

The quarter included $301 million of pretax tariff refund benefits, contributing $228 million to net earnings and $0.50 to both GAAP and adjusted EPS. The refunds relate to tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, the release said. Excluding them, GAAP EPS would have increased 42 percent and adjusted EPS 21 percent — an adjusted $2.15 that still beat the $2.05 consensus.

Operating income rose to $1.7 billion, from prior-year GAAP operating income of $0.9 billion, a margin rate of 6.2 percent including 1.1 percentage points of benefit from the refunds. The gross margin rate expanded to 30.5 percent from 28.2 percent; excluding the refunds it would have expanded about 1.2 percentage points, reflecting growth in non-merchandise sales and supply-chain productivity gains, partly offset by higher freight and fuel costs.

Cash returns, investment and raised guidance

Target spent $1.4 billion on capital expenditures in the quarter, $0.4 billion more than a year earlier, and expects to invest between $5 billion and $6 billion in 2027. It paid dividends of $527 million and repurchased $251 million of shares, retiring 1.6 million shares. Trailing-twelve-month return on invested capital was 16.5 percent, up from 13.4 percent.

Target now expects full-year 2026 net sales growth in a range around 6 percent, one percentage point higher than its prior guidance, an operating income margin rate around 6.2 percent, and GAAP and adjusted EPS of $10.65 to $11.40, up from the previous adjusted guidance range of $9.90 to $10.90 reported by Zacks. The new EPS range includes about $2.14 a share in tariff refund benefits recognized to date and excludes any potential future refunds. For the holidays, the company is leaning on value and exclusives — more than 8,000 new gifts, a $30 Thanksgiving meal for six, and early Black Friday savings and daily deals through December 24 — and said month-to-date November net sales are in line with guidance, accelerating from October trends. The holiday quarter will test the raised outlook.
